PROJECT 5ROBOTICS / VISION-LANGUAGE-ACTION

SmolVLA
Grasping.

A three-person final-year project: a dual-camera SO101 robot follows language instructions to pick a red or blue cube, place it in a target area and return to its starting pose.

PythonPyTorchLeRobotSmolVLA

Team project & contribution

I worked with the team on the grasp-and-place system using front and wrist cameras, and participated in demonstration collection, annotation and fine-tuning of the pretrained SmolVLA policy.

Runtime target switching

The same policy stays loaded when the target changes. The controller updates the task text, clears the active action chunk and rejects late inference results from the previous task before executing new predictions.

REAL-ROBOT DEMONSTRATIONS

Target selection & voice control

DEMONSTRATIONS / SAMPLING / FINE-TUNING

200 demonstrations

The team collected two-object demonstrations across five regions, swapping left/right colors and balancing red/blue target tasks. Each demonstration was marked at the frame immediately before continuous gripper closure.

Stage-aware sampling

Half of each batch is sampled from before the marker and half from the full trajectory, with red/blue tasks balanced. Each input retains 50 future recorded actions as supervision, covering carrying, placement and return.

Fine-tuning setup

The run used 160 training demonstrations and 40 validation demonstrations, a batch size of 128 and 7,500 optimizer updates to fine-tune pretrained SmolVLA.

Stage-aware sampling was an experimental training choice; its effect has not been isolated by a controlled comparison.

REPORTED REAL-ROBOT RESULT

Whole-task completion

17 / 2085% in familiar adjacent-object layouts

Success required placing the correct color in the target area and returning the arm. Autonomous retries counted as success; this is whole-task completion, rather than first-grasp accuracy.

Limits & evaluation scope

Trial-by-trial records remain to be consolidated. Changed spacing or diagonal layouts can cause approach errors, and reliable post-grasp target verification remains unresolved.

This result does not establish performance in unseen layouts or a measured improvement over a baseline.
